articles.content_en: Article 1 These Regulations are formulated to ensure that employees who suffer work-related accidents or contract occupational diseases receive medical treatment and economic compensation, to promote work-related injury prevention and occupational rehabilitation, and to spread the risk of work-related injuries among employers.

Article 2 Enterprises, public institutions, social organizations, private non-enterprise units, foundations, law firms, accounting firms and other organizations, and individual businesses with employees (hereinafter referred to as "employers") within the territory of the People's Republic of China shall participate in work-related injury insurance in accordance with the provisions of these Regulations and pay work-related injury insurance premiums for all their staff and workers or employees (hereinafter referred to as "employees").
All employees of enterprises, public institutions, social organizations, private non-enterprise units, foundations, law firms, accounting firms and other organizations, and employees of individual businesses within the territory of the People's Republic of China have the right to enjoy work-related injury insurance benefits in accordance with the provisions of these Regulations.

Article 3 The collection and payment of work-related injury insurance premiums shall be implemented in accordance with the provisions of the Interim Regulations on the Collection and Payment of Social Insurance Premiums concerning the collection and payment of basic old-age insurance premiums, basic medical insurance premiums, and unemployment insurance premiums.

Article 4 An employer shall make public within its entity the relevant information about its participation in work-related injury insurance.
Employers and employees shall comply with the laws and regulations concerning work safety and occupational disease prevention, implement safety and health regulations and standards, prevent work-related injury accidents, and avoid and reduce occupational disease hazards.
When an employee suffers a work-related injury, the employer shall take measures to ensure that the injured employee receives timely medical treatment.

Article 5 The social insurance administrative department of the State Council shall be responsible for the work of work-related injury insurance nationwide.
The social insurance administrative departments of local people's governments at or above the county level shall be responsible for the work of work-related injury insurance within their respective administrative regions.
The social insurance agencies (hereinafter referred to as "agencies") established by the social insurance administrative departments in accordance with the relevant provisions of the State Council shall specifically handle work-related injury insurance affairs.

Article 6 When formulating policies and standards for work-related injury insurance, the social insurance administrative department and other departments shall seek the opinions of trade union organizations and representatives of employers.

Article 7 The work-related injury insurance fund shall consist of work-related injury insurance premiums paid by employers, interest on the work-related injury insurance fund, and other funds lawfully incorporated into the work-related injury insurance fund.

Article 8 The rate of work-related injury insurance premiums shall be determined based on the principles of determining revenues based on expenditures and balancing revenues and expenditures.
The State shall determine differential rates for industries based on the degree of work-related injury risks of different industries, and shall determine several rate brackets within each industry based on factors such as the use of work-related injury insurance premiums and the incidence of work-related injuries. The differential rates for industries and the rate brackets within industries shall be formulated by the social insurance administrative department of the State Council and shall be promulgated and implemented after approval by the State Council.
The agency of the coordinated region shall, based on the employer's use of work-related injury insurance premiums and the incidence of work-related injuries, apply the corresponding rate bracket within the industry to which the employer belongs to determine the employer's contribution rate.

Article 9 The social insurance administrative department of the State Council shall regularly monitor the revenue and expenditure of work-related injury insurance funds in all coordinated regions nationwide, and shall timely propose a plan for adjusting the differential rates for industries and the rate brackets within industries, and shall report it to the State Council for approval before promulgation and implementation.

Article 10 Employers shall pay work-related injury insurance premiums on time. Individual employees shall not pay work-related injury insurance premiums.
The amount of work-related injury insurance premiums paid by an employer shall be the product of the total wages of its employees multiplied by the employer's contribution rate.
For industries where it is difficult to pay work-related injury insurance premiums based on total wages, the specific methods for paying work-related injury insurance premiums shall be prescribed by the social insurance administrative department of the State Council.

Article 11 The work-related injury insurance fund shall gradually achieve provincial-level pooling.
Industries with cross-regional operations and high mobility of production may participate in work-related injury insurance in the pooling region in a relatively centralized manner in a different locality. Specific measures shall be formulated by the social insurance administrative department of the State Council jointly with the competent departments of the relevant industries.

Article 12 The work-related injury insurance fund shall be deposited into the financial account for social security funds, and shall be used for the payment of work-related injury insurance benefits as provided for in these Regulations, expenses for labor capacity appraisal, expenses for publicity and training on work-related injury prevention, and other expenses for work-related injury insurance as provided for by laws and regulations.
The specific measures for the proportion, use, and management of the funds drawn for work-related injury prevention expenses shall be prescribed by the social insurance administrative department of the State Council jointly with the finance, health administration, and work safety supervision and management departments of the State Council.
No unit or individual may use the work-related injury insurance fund for investment and operation, construction or renovation of office premises, distribution of bonuses, or diversion to other purposes.

Article 13 The work-related injury insurance fund shall retain a certain proportion of reserve fund for the payment of work-related injury insurance benefits in the event of major accidents in the coordinated region; if the reserve fund is insufficient for such payment, the people's government of the coordinated region shall advance the payment. The specific proportion of the reserve fund to the total fund and the method for using the reserve fund shall be prescribed by the people's governments of provinces, autonomous regions, and municipalities directly under the Central Government.

Article 17 Where an employee suffers a work-related accident or is diagnosed or identified as having an occupational disease in accordance with the Law on the Prevention and Control of Occupational Diseases, the employer shall, within 30 days from the date of the occurrence of the accident or the date of diagnosis or identification of the occupational disease, file an application for work-related injury identification with the social insurance administrative department of the coordinated region. Under special circumstances, with the consent of the social insurance administrative department, the application period may be appropriately extended.
If the employer fails to file the application for work-related injury identification in accordance with the provisions of the preceding paragraph, the injured employee or his/her close relatives, or the trade union organization may, within one year from the date of the occurrence of the accident or the date of diagnosis or identification of the occupational disease, directly file an application for work-related injury identification with the social insurance administrative department of the coordinated region where the employer is located.
Matters that shall be subject to work-related injury identification by the provincial social insurance administrative department in accordance with the provisions of the first paragraph of this Article shall, based on the principle of territoriality, be handled by the social insurance administrative department of the city divided into districts where the employer is located.
If the employer fails to submit the application for work-related injury identification within the time limit specified in the first paragraph of this Article, the expenses for work-related injury benefits and other related expenses that occur during this period and are in compliance with the provisions of these Regulations shall be borne by the employer.

Article 19 After accepting an application for work-related injury identification, the social insurance administrative department may, based on review needs, conduct investigation and verification of the accident injury. The employer, employees, trade union organizations, medical institutions, and relevant departments shall assist in such investigation. The diagnosis of occupational diseases and the appraisal of diagnostic disputes shall be carried out in accordance with the relevant provisions of the Law on the Prevention and Control of Occupational Diseases. For an occupational disease diagnosis certificate or occupational disease diagnosis appraisal certificate lawfully obtained, the social insurance administrative department shall not conduct further investigation or verification.
If an employee or his/her close relatives consider the injury to be a work-related injury, but the employer does not, the employer shall bear the burden of adducing evidence.

Article 20 The social insurance administrative department shall make a decision on work-related injury identification within 60 days from the date of accepting the application for work-related injury identification, and shall notify in writing the employee who applied for work-related injury identification or his/her close relatives and the employer of the employee.
The social insurance administrative department shall, for an application for work-related injury identification that is accepted and where the facts are clear and the rights and obligations are definite, make a decision on work-related injury identification within 15 days.
If the decision on work-related injury identification needs to be based on the conclusions of a judicial organ or the relevant competent administrative department, the time limit for making the decision on work-related injury identification shall be suspended during the period when the judicial organ or the relevant competent administrative department has not yet reached a conclusion.
Staff members of the social insurance administrative department who have an interest in the applicant for work-related injury identification shall withdraw from the matter.

Article 21 Where an employee suffers a work-related injury and, after treatment, the injury becomes relatively stable and there is disability affecting the capacity for work, a labor capacity appraisal shall be conducted.

Article 22 Labor capacity appraisal means the grading appraisal of the degree of labor dysfunction and the degree of inability to perform daily self-care.
Labor dysfunction is divided into ten disability grades, the most severe being Grade 1 and the least severe being Grade 10.
Inability to perform daily self-care is divided into three grades: complete inability to perform daily self-care, major inability to perform daily self-care, and partial inability to perform daily self-care.
The standards for labor capacity appraisal shall be formulated by the social insurance administrative department of the State Council jointly with the health administrative department of the State Council and other departments.

Article 23 An application for labor capacity appraisal shall be filed with the labor capacity appraisal committee of the city divided into districts by the employer, the employee with work-related injury, or his close relatives, and the decision on work-related injury determination and relevant materials on the employee's medical treatment for the work-related injury shall be provided.

Article 24 The labor capacity appraisal committee of a province, autonomous region, or municipality directly under the Central Government and that of a city divided into districts shall respectively be composed of representatives from the social insurance administrative department, the health administrative department, the trade union organization, the handling agency, and the employer at the corresponding level.
The labor capacity appraisal committee shall establish a medical and health expert database. Medical and health professionals included in the expert database shall meet the following conditions:
(1) having senior professional technical position qualifications in medical and health care;
(2) mastering relevant knowledge of labor capacity appraisal; and
(3) having good professional ethics.

Article 25 After receiving an application for labor capacity appraisal, the labor capacity appraisal committee of a city divided into districts shall randomly select three or five relevant experts from the medical and health expert database established by it to form an expert panel, which shall provide appraisal opinions. The labor capacity appraisal committee of the city divided into districts shall, on the basis of the appraisal opinions of the expert panel, make a labor capacity appraisal conclusion for the employee with work-related injury; if necessary, it may entrust a qualified medical institution to assist in conducting relevant diagnoses.
The labor capacity appraisal committee of the city divided into districts shall make a labor capacity appraisal conclusion within 60 days from the date of receiving the application for labor capacity appraisal; if necessary, the time limit for making the labor capacity appraisal conclusion may be extended by 30 days. The labor capacity appraisal conclusion shall be served in a timely manner to the entity and individual that applied for the appraisal.

Article 26 Where the entity or individual that applied for the appraisal disagrees with the appraisal conclusion made by the labor capacity appraisal committee of a city divided into districts, it may file an application for re-appraisal with the labor capacity appraisal committee of the province, autonomous region, or municipality directly under the Central Government within 15 days from the date of receiving the said appraisal conclusion. The labor capacity appraisal conclusion made by the labor capacity appraisal committee of the province, autonomous region, or municipality directly under the Central Government shall be the final conclusion.

Article 27 The labor capacity appraisal work shall be objective and impartial. Where a member of the labor capacity appraisal committee or an expert participating in the appraisal has an interest in the party, he shall withdraw.

Article 28 One year after the date on which a labor capacity appraisal conclusion is made, where the employee with work-related injury or his close relatives, the entity where he works, or the handling agency believes that the disability condition has changed, they may apply for a review appraisal of labor capacity.

Article 29 The time limit for a labor capacity appraisal committee to conduct a re-appraisal and a review appraisal in accordance with Articles 26 and 28 of these Regulations shall be implemented in accordance with the provisions of paragraph 2 of Article 25 of these Regulations.

Article 30 Where an employee suffers an accident injury at work or contracts an occupational disease and receives medical treatment, he shall enjoy work-related injury medical treatment benefits.
An employee receiving medical treatment for a work-related injury shall be treated in a medical institution that has signed a service agreement; in an emergency, he may first receive emergency treatment at a nearby medical institution.
Expenses incurred for medical treatment of a work-related injury that are covered by the catalogue of work-related injury insurance medical treatment items, the catalogue of work-related injury insurance medicines, and the standards for work-related injury insurance hospitalization services shall be paid from the work-related injury insurance fund. The catalogue of work-related injury insurance medical treatment items, the catalogue of work-related injury insurance medicines, and the standards for work-related injury insurance hospitalization services shall be prescribed by the social insurance administrative department of the State Council jointly with the health administrative department of the State Council, the food and drug regulatory department, and other departments.
Subsidies for meals during hospitalization for treatment of a work-related injury, as well as the transportation, accommodation, and meal expenses incurred by an employee with work-related injury for medical treatment outside the overall planning region, as certified by the medical institution and approved by the handling agency, shall be paid from the work-related injury insurance fund. The specific standards for payment by the fund shall be prescribed by the people's government of the overall planning region.
Where an employee with work-related injury receives treatment for a disease not caused by the work-related injury, he shall not enjoy work-related injury medical treatment benefits, and such treatment shall be handled in accordance with the basic medical insurance provisions.
Expenses for work-related injury rehabilitation of an employee with work-related injury at a medical institution that has signed a service agreement shall be paid from the work-related injury insurance fund if they comply with the provisions.

Article 31 Where an administrative reconsideration or administrative action occurs after the social insurance administrative department makes a decision recognizing a work-related injury, the payment of medical expenses for the employee's work-related injury treatment shall not be suspended during the period of administrative reconsideration or administrative action.

Article 32 Where an employee with work-related injury needs, for daily life or employment purposes, and confirmed by the labor capacity appraisal committee, to install prostheses, orthoses, artificial eyes, artificial teeth, and configure wheelchairs and other assistive devices, the necessary expenses shall be paid from the work-related injury insurance fund in accordance with the standards prescribed by the State.

Article 33 Where an employee suffers an accident injury at work or contracts an occupational disease and needs to suspend work to receive medical treatment for the work-related injury, his original wage and welfare benefits shall remain unchanged during the period of suspension of work with pay, and shall be paid monthly by the entity where he works.
The period of suspension of work with pay shall generally not exceed 12 months. If the injury is severe or the circumstances are special, upon confirmation by the labor capacity appraisal committee of the city divided into districts, the period may be appropriately extended, but the extension shall not exceed 12 months. After the employee with work-related injury has been assessed with a disability grade, the original benefits shall be discontinued, and he shall enjoy disability benefits in accordance with the relevant provisions of this Chapter. If the employee with work-related injury still needs medical treatment after the expiration of the period of suspension of work with pay, he shall continue to enjoy work-related injury medical treatment benefits.
If an employee with work-related injury who is unable to take care of himself in daily life needs nursing care during the period of suspension of work with pay, the entity where he works shall be responsible for such care.

Article 34 Where an employee with work-related injury has been assessed with a disability grade and confirmed by the labor capacity appraisal committee to need nursing care in daily life, a monthly living care allowance shall be paid from the work-related injury insurance fund.
The living care allowance shall be paid according to the three different grades, namely complete inability to perform daily self-care, major inability to perform daily self-care, and partial inability to perform daily self-care, and the standards shall be respectively 50%, 40%, or 30% of the average monthly wage of employees in the overall planning region in the preceding year.

Article 36 Where an employee is assessed as having Grade 5 or Grade 6 disabilities due to a work-related injury, he shall enjoy the following benefits:
(1) A lump-sum disability subsidy shall be paid from the work-related injury insurance fund according to the disability grade, the standards being: 18 months of his own wage for Grade 5 disability, and 16 months of his own wage for Grade 6 disability;
(2) The labor relationship with the employer shall be retained, and the employer shall arrange suitable work. If it is difficult to arrange work, the employer shall pay a monthly disability allowance to the employee, the standards being: 70% of his own wage for Grade 5 disability, and 60% of his own wage for Grade 6 disability, and the employer shall, in accordance with the provisions, pay all social insurance premiums payable for him. If the actual amount of the disability allowance is lower than the local minimum wage standard, the difference shall be made up by the employer.
Upon the proposal of the employee with work-related injury, the employee may dissolve or terminate the labor relationship with the employer, and a lump-sum medical subsidy for work-related injury shall be paid from the work-related injury insurance fund, and a lump-sum employment subsidy for disability shall be paid by the employer. The specific standards for the lump-sum medical subsidy for work-related injury and the lump-sum employment subsidy for disability shall be prescribed by the people's governments of provinces, autonomous regions, and municipalities directly under the Central Government.

Article 38 Where the work-related injury of an employee with work-related injury recurs and is confirmed to need treatment, he shall enjoy the work-related injury benefits provided in Articles 30, 32, and 33 of these Regulations.

Article 40 The disability allowance, the pension for the dependents of the deceased, and the living care allowance shall be adjusted in a timely manner by the social insurance administrative department of the overall planning region based on changes in the average wage of employees and living expenses and other circumstances. The adjustment method shall be prescribed by the people's governments of provinces, autonomous regions, and municipalities directly under the Central Government.

Article 41 Where a worker is involved in an accident during a business trip or goes missing while engaging in emergency rescue or disaster relief, the wages shall be paid as usual within three months from the month when the accident occurs, and shall be suspended from the fourth month. Instead, the work-related injury insurance fund shall pay monthly dependency allowances to the dependents. If the dependents have financial difficulties, they may receive an advance payment of 50% of the lump-sum bereavement subsidy. Where the worker is declared dead by a People's Court, the matter shall be handled in accordance with the provisions of Article 39 of these Regulations concerning death from work-related injury.

Article 43 Where an employer is divided, merged, or transferred, the surviving entity shall assume the work-related injury insurance responsibilities of the original employer; if the original employer has participated in work-related injury insurance, the surviving entity shall go through the modification registration of work-related injury insurance with the local agency.
Where an employer contracts out its operations, the work-related injury insurance responsibilities shall be assumed by the entity with which the worker has a labor relationship.
Where a worker suffers from a work-related injury during a secondment, the original employer shall assume the work-related injury insurance responsibilities, but the original employer and the seconding entity may agree on the method of compensation.
Where an enterprise is bankrupt, the expenses for work-related injury insurance benefits that shall be paid by the entity shall be allocated according to law during the bankruptcy liquidation.

Article 44 Where a worker is dispatched to work overseas, if the worker shall participate in the local work-related injury insurance in accordance with the laws of the destination country or region, the worker shall participate in such local insurance, and the domestic work-related injury insurance relationship shall be suspended; if the worker cannot participate in the local work-related injury insurance, the domestic work-related injury insurance relationship shall not be suspended.

Article 45 Where a worker suffers from a recurrence of work-related injury and shall be entitled to disability allowance according to the provisions, the worker shall enjoy the disability allowance benefits based on the newly assessed disability grade.

Article 47 The agency shall conclude service agreements with medical institutions and assistive device fitting institutions on the basis of equal consultation, and shall publish the list of medical institutions and assistive device fitting institutions that have concluded service agreements. The specific measures shall be formulated by the social insurance administrative department of the State Council jointly with the health administrative department of the State Council, the civil affairs department, and other relevant departments.

Article 48 The agency shall, in accordance with the agreement and the relevant national catalogues and standards, verify the use of medical expenses, rehabilitation expenses, and assistive device expenses for workers with work-related injuries, and shall settle the expenses in full and on time.

Article 49 The agency shall periodically publish the revenue and expenditure of the work-related injury insurance fund, and shall timely submit suggestions on adjusting the premium rates to the social insurance administrative department.

Article 50 The social insurance administrative department and the agency shall periodically solicit opinions from workers with work-related injuries, medical institutions, assistive device fitting institutions, and all sectors of society on improving work-related injury insurance work.

Article 51 The social insurance administrative department shall, according to law, supervise and inspect the collection of work-related injury insurance premiums and the payment of the work-related injury insurance fund.
The finance department and audit authorities shall, according to law, supervise the revenue, expenditure, and management of the work-related injury insurance fund.

Article 52 Any organization or individual shall have the right to report any illegal act concerning work-related injury insurance. The social insurance administrative department shall promptly investigate the report, handle it in accordance with the provisions, and keep the reporter's identity confidential.

Article 53 Trade union organizations shall, according to law, protect the legitimate rights and interests of workers with work-related injuries, and exercise supervision over the work-related injury insurance work of employers.
Article 54 Disputes between a worker and an employer concerning work-related injury insurance benefits shall be handled in accordance with the relevant provisions on handling labor disputes.

Article 56 Where any entity or individual misappropriates the work-related injury insurance fund in violation of Article 12 of these Regulations, if the act constitutes a crime, criminal liability shall be investigated according to law; if the act does not constitute a crime, a sanction or disciplinary sanction shall be imposed according to law. The misappropriated fund shall be recovered by the social insurance administrative department and be incorporated into the work-related injury insurance fund; the illegal gains confiscated shall be turned over to the State Treasury according to law.

Article 59 Where a medical institution or assistive device fitting institution fails to provide services in accordance with the service agreement, the agency may terminate the service agreement.
Where the agency fails to settle expenses in full and on time, the social insurance administrative department shall order it to make corrections; the medical institution or assistive device fitting institution may terminate the service agreement.

Article 60 Where an employer, a worker with work-related injury, or his close relative fraudulently obtains work-related injury insurance benefits, or a medical institution or assistive device fitting institution fraudulently obtains payments from the work-related injury insurance fund, the social insurance administrative department shall order the return of the obtained amounts and impose a fine of not less than two times but not more than five times the amount fraudulently obtained; if the circumstances are serious and constitute a crime, criminal liability shall be investigated according to law.

Article 62 Where an employer that shall participate in work-related injury insurance in accordance with these Regulations fails to do so, the social insurance administrative department shall order it to participate within a specified period, pay the work-related injury insurance premiums that shall be paid, and charge a late payment surcharge at an additional rate of 0.05% per day from the date the premiums become overdue; if the employer still fails to pay upon expiration of the specified period, it shall be fined not less than one time but not more than three times the overdue amount.
Where an employee of an employer that shall participate in work-related injury insurance in accordance with these Regulations but fails to do so suffers a work-related injury, the employer shall pay the expenses in accordance with the items and standards of work-related injury insurance benefits provided for in these Regulations.
After the employer participates in work-related injury insurance and pays the overdue work-related injury insurance premiums and late payment surcharges, the newly incurred expenses shall be paid by the work-related injury insurance fund and the employer in accordance with the provisions of these Regulations.

Article 63 Where an employer violates the provisions of Article 19 of these Regulations and refuses to assist the social insurance administrative department in investigating and verifying an accident, the social insurance administrative department shall order correction and impose a fine of not less than RMB 2,000 yuan but not more than RMB 20,000 yuan.

Article 64 The term "total wages" as used in these Regulations means the total amount of labor remuneration directly paid by an employer to all its employees.
The term "personal wages" as used in these Regulations means the average monthly contribution-based wages of an employee suffering from a work-related injury for the 12 months preceding the occurrence of the accident injury or the diagnosis of an occupational disease due to work. If the personal wages are higher than 300% of the average wages of employees in the pooling region, they shall be calculated as 300% of the average wages of employees in the pooling region; if the personal wages are lower than 60% of the average wages of employees in the pooling region, they shall be calculated as 60% of the average wages of employees in the pooling region.

Article 65 Where a public servant or a staff member of a public institution or social organization managed with reference to the Civil Servant Law suffers an accident injury or contracts an occupational disease due to work, the expenses shall be paid by the employing entity. The specific measures shall be formulated by the social insurance administrative department of the State Council jointly with the finance department of the State Council.

Article 66 Where an employee of an entity without a business license or that has not been registered or filed according to law, or an entity whose business license has been revoked or whose registration or filing has been canceled according to law, suffers an accident injury or contracts an occupational disease, the entity shall pay a lump-sum compensation to the injured or disabled employee or the close relatives of the deceased employee, and the compensation standard shall not be lower than the work-related injury insurance benefits provided for in these Regulations; an employer shall not use child labor, and if an employer uses child labor and causes the child laborer to become disabled or die, the entity shall pay a lump-sum compensation to the child laborer or the close relatives of the deceased child laborer, and the compensation standard shall not be lower than the work-related injury insurance benefits provided for in these Regulations. The specific measures shall be formulated by the social insurance administrative department of the State Council.
Where a dispute arises between the entity and the close relatives of the injured, disabled or deceased employee specified in the preceding paragraph regarding the amount of compensation, or where a dispute arises between the entity and the child laborer or the close relatives of the deceased child laborer specified in the preceding paragraph regarding the amount of compensation, the matter shall be handled in accordance with the relevant provisions on handling labor disputes.

Article 67 These Regulations shall come into force as of January 1, 2004. Where an employee who suffered an accident injury or contracted an occupational disease before these Regulations came into force has not yet completed the work-related injury determination, the matter shall be handled in accordance with the provisions of these Regulations.
